
  Check an API spec (OpenAPI 3.x) and write its diagnostics to stderr, writing no IR anywhere.
  validate is compile's pipeline with the document dropped instead of marshalled, for a gate that
  wants the diagnostics and the exit code and would throw the document away.

  The diagnostics and the exit code are compile's: 0 when nothing reaches --fail-on, 1 when
  something does or the spec lowered to no document at all, 2 for a misuse or an I/O error.

  --skip-validate names the referential-integrity pass, not this command: it drops that pass's
  diagnostics and keeps the compiler's.

  --opt is compile's, and takes the same settings: a spec that needs one to compile needs it here
  too, or what is checked is not what would be built.

  USAGE

    morphic validate <spec-file> [--flags]

  EXAMPLES

    # diagnostics and exit code only
    morphic validate openapi.yaml

    # a stricter gate: exit 1 on a warning too
    morphic validate openapi.yaml --fail-on warning

  FLAGS

    --fail-on        Exit 1 on diagnostics at or above this severity: error or warning (error)
    -h --help        Help for validate
    --opt            Set one key=value option on the compiler the spec selects (repeatable)
    --skip-validate  Skip the referential-integrity validate pass
